recommendation: Keep the audit commit. The current spec source already expresses the requested rule; any remaining runtime acceptance of id-only elements should be handled in validator/tooling follow-up rather than by changing the FHIR source.
issue_request: FHIR-15964 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core change request, raised in STU3 and applied for R5, asking that an IG element such as <package id="foo"/> be invalid rather than accepted by validation.
initial_application: No FHIR-15964-tagged source commit was found. FHIR-I minutes from 2019-12-02 record the issue as already applied by a tooling update, and the relevant ele-1 source/history already excluded Element.id from satisfying the content-required invariant.
additional_context: A 2022 Zulip thread revisited the issue because of normative-break concerns, but Lloyd McKenzie stated that the current ele-1 invariant already fixed it. Later same-invariant changes, including FHIR-43103 wording clarification and FHIR-26565's empty Parameters exception, preserve the id-only exclusion for ordinary elements.
reconciliation: No source was changed. source/datatypes/element.xml is active through source/fhir.ini and defines ele-1 as hasValue() or (children().count() > id.count()) or $this is Parameters; its XML XPath also does not count an XML id attribute as content.

related_jiras.note: Changed the same ele-1 invariant to allow empty Parameters while preserving the id-only exclusion for ordinary elements.
Clarified the ele-1 human wording to say 'or both' without changing the id-only rule.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive FHIR-core issue asking that an element with only Element.id be rejected by validation.
evidence_items.learned: This establishes final WG intent that id-only elements should be invalid.

evidence_items.summary: The active Element invariant uses hasValue() or (children().count() > id.count()) or $this is Parameters, and the XML XPath omits the XML id attribute.
evidence_items.learned: The current build source already rejects id-only ordinary elements.
